paras: The threatened lynching of Fat Ward took place at Greer, South Carolina, on the night of Sunday, August 15, 1915, when a mob gathered outside the town lockup where Ward, a Black man, was held after a shooting during his arrest. A doctor and a town officer drove him to the Spartanburg jail before the crowd acted.

According to a Spartanburg dispatch, Ward bore "the reputation of being a desperate character" and was "alleged to have a criminal court record in Greenville county." Both reports said he had been causing trouble throughout the day before his arrest.

At about 9 o'clock on Sunday night, town officers surrounded Ward to arrest him, and the dispatch said, with the qualifier "it is said," that he fired five shots, none of which hit anyone. A bullet passed through his shoulder at the same time, though the report did not say who fired it. Once it became known that Dr. W. T. Brockman was treating him, a crowd collected outside the lockup, "bent, it is said, on taking vengeance for an attack on the town officers."

Brockman and Officer Charles Littlefield then put Ward in an automobile and sped toward Spartanburg before the crowd learned of their plan. Ward reached the Spartanburg jail early on Monday, August 16.
No arrests of members of the crowd, and no later report of charges or a trial for Ward, appear in the coverage.

The Sumter Watchman and Southron printed the Spartanburg dispatch on August 21 under the headline "NEGRO ESCAPES MOB" with the subhead "Finds Safety in Jail at Spartanburg." It relayed the officers' version with repeated hedges and named the crowd's aim, vengeance, without comment. Two days earlier the Bamberg Herald had given it one sentence in a state-news column: Ward "had to be spirited away to jail to prevent summary vengeance being wrought on him."
No Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

The Spartanburg dispatch placed the arrest at Greer on Sunday night, while the Bamberg Herald gave Monday and "Spartanburg county," probably conflating the arrest with Ward's removal to the Spartanburg jail.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Fat Ward
bases: A mob gathered outside the Greer lockup intending 'vengeance' on a Black prisoner, who was removed to another jail before it acted; no one was killed (A3, A1).

No one was killed: Ward was taken to the Spartanburg jail before the crowd outside the Greer lockup could act (A3, A1). The crowd, without lawful authority, sought vengeance for his alleged attack on officers, so this is a threatened lynching only (A3).

Only the Aug. 16 Spartanburg dispatch gives details (A3); the Bamberg paragraph shares its wording ('trouble throughout the day') and appears to be condensed from the same report rather than an independent account (A1).

accounts.label: Spartanburg dispatch (officers' version)
accounts.gist: Ward had caused trouble all day and fired five shots when officers surrounded him at about 9 p.m.; a crowd gathered once it learned he was being treated, and he was driven to Spartanburg before it knew.

accounts.label: State-news roundup
accounts.gist: After a day of trouble Ward was arrested in Spartanburg county on Monday and spirited to jail to prevent summary vengeance.

framing.detail: The Watchman and Southron headlined 'NEGRO ESCAPES MOB' and 'Finds Safety in Jail at Spartanburg', called Ward 'a desperate character' and passed on the officers' account with 'it is said'.
The Bamberg Herald ran one sentence among unrelated state news, saying Ward had to be spirited away 'to prevent summary vengeance being wrought on him'.
